acceptance: The schema is generated, not hand-written; one command regenerates it, and a drift check wired into required CI fails when the schema and the validator disagree.
Every bundle under results-data/bundles validates against it, and a bundle with a required key removed fails.
The schema carries the result schema version and is published at a stable URL through the site-inputs bundle; the docs state which changes are compatible within major version 2.
The published schema reference page describes the current version, with the legacy page marked as legacy.
make duplicate-check-delta shows no new duplicate of existing validation logic, and a changelog.d fragment is present.
context:
Origin: adversarial review of an agent-facing strategy for BenchBox, 2026-11-12. Owner decisions quoted here were made on that date. Line numbers are hints; re-read the cited file before relying on them.

Prior decision to respect: results_schema.json is listed under removed_legacy in the Explorer build contract. That file described the Explorer's DuckDB read model, not the bundle. Use a different name and path, and state in the PR that this does not reverse that removal.

Decision gate: read the gate ruling first; on no-go, do nothing and ask the owner to drop the item. On go, first decide and record whether the validator is refactored to read the schema or the schema is emitted from the validator; if neither can be done without two definitions, stop and report. Result-schema code may be a soundness path that needs the external reviewer.

Verification rubric: pass only if the drift check is shown failing on a deliberate mismatch and the whole corpus validates.

Guardrails: work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone. Related items are delivered together on one feature branch and one PR, as their umbrella item names (site work: BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site); squash-merged. Add a changelog.d fragment for any user-facing change. No live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers) runs only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status. Follow the comment policy (make comment-policy-check). Stop and report instead of widening scope; scope removed during review must be re-homed to a named item or dropped by the owner with a reason.

Review note (2026-11-13): if bundle-record-host-load-20261113 has landed, the schema must cover its fields.

Revision (2026-11-13), after an independent critique and owner decisions: deferred; the earlier gate could have passed this item on code reading alone.
description:
Problem: the result bundle is at schema version 2.4 and is defined only in Python (build_result_payload and SchemaV2Validator in benchbox/core/results/schema.py, key orders in schema_specs.yaml). No JSON Schema is published, so a pipeline or agent that parses a bundle has nothing to validate against, and the public schema page describes legacy version 1.1.

Outcome: a JSON Schema for the current bundle version, generated from the same source the validator uses, published at a stable URL with a stated compatibility promise.

Blocked: deferred until agent-demand-signals-baseline-20261113 reports, or the owner unblocks it.

Non-goals: no change to the bundle's shape; no hand-maintained second definition.
